kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.canonical_name: 5 mm through-hole LED (light emitting diode), assorted colors
identity.manufacturer: generic / unbranded (no LED manufacturer is named in ELEGOO's kit documentation)
identity.manufacturer_part_number: generic (no specific MPN found; treated as a commodity part)
generic_equivalents: Adafruit 4203 diffused 5mm LED pack (used here as a reference part for price and specs)
any standard T-1 3/4 5mm through-hole indicator LED, e.g. Kingbright or Lite-On equivalents

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small light that turns on when current flows through it the correct way, glowing a single color such as red, yellow, green, or blue.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Used as a simple visual indicator or status light in a circuit, for example to show that a button was pressed, a sensor was triggered, or a program reached a certain step. In the Arduino starter kit it is one of the first parts used to learn digital output.
function.how_it_works_briefly: An LED is a diode, a part that only lets current flow in one direction. When current flows from the anode (positive lead) to the cathode (negative lead) and the voltage across it reaches the LED's forward voltage (the minimum voltage needed to turn it on), the semiconductor inside emits light. Because an LED's resistance drops sharply once it is lit, it must always be wired in series with a resistor to limit the current, otherwise too much current flows and can damage the LED or the pin driving it.

pinout.name: anode
pinout.notes: The longer of the two leads on a new, untrimmed LED.

pinout.name: cathode
pinout.role: negative terminal, current exits here (to ground)
pinout.notes: The shorter lead. Also marked by a flat-ground spot on the rim of the plastic dome on the same side as this lead, useful once leads have been trimmed or bent.

pins.pin_1_identification: Hold the LED with both leads visible: the longer lead is the anode (positive). If the leads have been trimmed to equal length, look instead for a flat spot ground into the rim of the clear plastic dome; the lead closest to that flat side is the cathode (negative).

electrical.operating_voltage: Forward voltage depends on color. A reference 5mm LED datasheet (components101) gives: red 1.63-2.03V, orange 2.03-2.10V, yellow 2.10-2.18V, green 1.9-4.0V, blue 2.48-3.7V, white 3.2-3.6V. A simpler reference from Adafruit's equivalent diffused 5mm LED pack states approximately 2.0V for red/yellow/green and approximately 3.3V for blue/white, both at 20mA. Treat red/yellow/green as roughly 2V and blue/white as roughly 3.3V for quick series-resistor math.
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: Not confirmed by sources consulted; not published for this generic part. Do not exceed the forward voltage rating in the forward direction, and avoid applying more than a few volts in reverse.
electrical.max_current: 30 mA forward current (components101 generic 5mm LED reference)
electrical.logic_level: Not a logic device itself; typically driven from a 5V Arduino Uno digital output pin through a series resistor, which limits current rather than the LED clamping to a logic level.

key_specs.package_size: 5mm diameter dome, roughly 8-9mm tall, T-1 3/4 through-hole package
key_specs.kit_colors_confirmed_by_sources: ELEGOO's own kit parts list (Electronix Express retailer listing and a CMU course parts list) shows 5 red, 5 yellow, 5 green, and 5 blue single-color LEDs (20 total), plus 1-2 separate 4-pin RGB LEDs. No white 5mm LED was found in either sourced parts list.
key_specs.forward_voltage_by_color_generic_datashe: red 1.63-2.03V, orange 2.03-2.10V, yellow 2.10-2.18V, green 1.9-4.0V, blue 2.48-3.7V, white 3.2-3.6V (components101)
key_specs.forward_voltage_simplified: ~2.0V for red/yellow/green, ~3.3V for blue/white, both at 20mA (Adafruit reference part)
key_specs.typical_luminous_intensity: ~250 mcd typical, diffused lens (Adafruit reference part; ELEGOO's own brightness spec was not published in sources checked)

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Small clear or tinted plastic dome about 5mm across and roughly 8-9mm tall, with two thin metal leads extending from the flat bottom.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Body tint often hints at the emitted color (clear, red, yellow, green, or blue tinted plastic), though some are water-clear regardless of color. One side of the dome's base rim has a flat-ground spot marking the cathode (negative) lead. No printed text or part number appears on the LED body itself.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: None on the part itself; any labeling is on the kit's storage bag or bin, not the component.
easily_confused_with: The kit's RGB LED, which looks like a similar 5mm dome but has 4 leads instead of 2 (one common anode or cathode plus three color leads)
IR emitters or phototransistors, which can look identical from the outside but are not visible-light indicators
A different color LED of the same kit when unlit, since some are water-clear until powered

example_connections.uno_pin: digital pin (e.g. pin 13) through a 220-330 ohm series resistor

required_extra_parts: series current-limiting resistor, commonly 220 ohm to 330 ohm for 5V logic
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: None required. Drive it directly with digitalWrite() for on/off, or analogWrite() on a PWM-capable pin for dimming.

hazards: Very low voltage and current, not a shock or fire hazard under normal use
Driving the LED without a series resistor lets too much current flow, which can burn out the LED almost instantly and can also damage the Arduino pin driving it
Reverse voltages beyond the part's rating can damage the LED, though this is a minor risk at 5V logic levels
handling_notes: Leads are thin wire and can fatigue or snap if bent back and forth repeatedly; bend gently near the base of the leads, not right where they enter the plastic body
Always wire a series resistor between the LED and the supply or digital pin; never connect an LED directly across 5V with no resistor
Static discharge is not a significant concern for a plain LED, unlike logic ICs in the same kit
common_mistakes: Wiring it backwards (anode and cathode swapped), so it simply stays dark since the diode blocks reverse current
Forgetting the series resistor, which over-drives the LED and can destroy it within seconds
Grabbing the kit's 4-pin RGB LED by mistake when a single-color 2-pin LED is needed, or vice versa

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: LED does not light at all
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Reversed polarity (anode and cathode swapped), an open circuit, or a burned-out LED
symptoms_and_causes.check: Flip the LED's orientation in the breadboard; confirm continuity and orientation with a multimeter's diode-test mode

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: LED lit briefly then went dark and stays dark
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Missing or undersized series resistor caused an overcurrent failure
symptoms_and_causes.check: Verify a resistor of the correct value is actually in series with the LED, not accidentally in parallel or omitted

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: LED is dim compared to others of the same color in the kit
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Series resistor value too high, or a partially degraded LED
symptoms_and_causes.check: Measure the resistor's actual value and compare against the intended design value; swap in a known-good LED of the same color to compare brightness

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to diode-test mode (the diode symbol). Touch the red probe to the anode (long lead) and the black probe to the cathode (short lead / flat-side lead); a healthy LED will glow faintly and the display will show a forward voltage drop reading (commonly in the 1.6V to 3.6V range depending on color). Swapping the probes should show no reading (open circuit) in the reverse direction, which confirms the part behaves as a diode rather than being shorted or open.

typical_suppliers: bundled only, not sold separately, by ELEGOO

confidence.notes: Two independent sources for the ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit's own parts list (an Electronix Express retailer listing and a CMU course resource page) both show the kit's single-color LEDs as 5 red + 5 yellow + 5 green + 5 blue = 20 pieces, with no white LED, plus 1-2 separate 4-pin RGB LEDs counted apart from this record. Neither source lists a white LED or a total of 25 single-color LEDs, so the seed record's '25 qty' and 'white' color could not be confirmed and may reflect a different kit revision or a mix-up with the separate RGB LED count; quantity_in_kit is set to 25 per task instruction despite this gap. Forward voltage figures vary noticeably between the generic components101 datasheet reference and the Adafruit reference part, especially for green (1.9-4.0V vs ~2V), so treat the 'simplified' 2V/3.3V grouping as the more practical field number and the wider range as the full spread across manufacturers. No manufacturer or MPN could be found for ELEGOO's actual bundled LEDs; this is a generic commodity part. Unit price is from an Adafruit 25-pack of equivalent diffused 5mm LEDs ($4.95 / 25 = $0.198, rounded to $0.20 per unit), not a price for ELEGOO's exact bundled part, since ELEGOO does not sell these LEDs separately. Absolute maximum reverse voltage was not found in any source checked and is left unconfirmed rather than guessed.
